standard_profile.notes: Leader-selected settings from 68 completed rows of the stopped partial development study. The runner enforces the chosen engine wall cap independently of native work budgets. Admission precedes the cap; final checking and packaging follow it. A timeout returns the best checked incumbent after fresh rechecks, if one exists. GPU work and other jobs loaded the machine; recorded timings are treated as upper bounds for quieter-machine planning, not guaranteed quiet-run limits. Measured engine settings are preserved exactly, including the ladder allowances.
reasoning: The user stopped this study after 68 of 256 expected jobs and explicitly selected these fixed profiles. This decision overrides the automatic incomplete-study recommendation, while completeness remains false.

Standard uses the measured 300/100 settings: no rule 9/9 full passes, mean 86.33333333333333 lifts; binding-rule arm 5/8 full passes, mean 65.0 lifts. Relative to available default pairs it loses 0/8 no-rule and 0/4 rule passes; paired mean extra lifts are +11.0 on 8 no-rule common passes and -1.0 on 4 rule common passes.

Live uses the measured 120/40 settings: no rule 7/9 full passes, mean 89.28571428571429 lifts; binding-rule arm 3/9 full passes, mean 67.66666666666667 lifts. Relative to available default pairs it loses 1/8 no-rule and 2/4 rule passes; paired mean extra lifts are +14.714285714285714 on 7 no-rule common passes and 0.0 on 2 rule common passes.

The 60/20 arm loses 3/8 no-rule and 3/4 rule default passes, with +12.6 lifts on 5 no-rule common passes and 0.0 on 1 rule common pass. Shorter budgets have a measured pass cost; passing-only cell means use different subsets and must not be compared directly.

Hard walls of 720 s live and 1800 s standard are explicit operational choices. Several observed engine durations and first-legal times exceed them; these measurements do not establish pass rates under the newly selected hard walls.

The 300 no-rule median total was 691.2326064159861 s and maximum 1715.4894255829859 s; with the rule median total was 1688.5506568124983 s and maximum 3089.9465782920015 s. For 120 no-rule, maximum first-legal time was 1022.9371175420238 s and maximum total was 1280.984540000034 s; these are different milestones.

Use loaded-machine timings as conservative upper-bound planning inputs per the user; a quiet-machine improvement is expected but unmeasured. No controlled comparison establishes a guaranteed upper bound.
